JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  COMMON ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) Heard Ms. Vaishali K. Kaladagi,
learned counsel for the appellant in MFA 101224 of 2021, who is also representing respondent No.2 in the connected appeal as well as Sri Manjunath Jadai, learned counsel for the respondent in MFA 101224 of 2021, who is representing the appellant in the connected appeal.
2. These two appeals are the outcome of the award that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-III, Ballari in MVC 1138 of 2016 dated 04.10.2019.

While the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (hereinafter be referred to as 'the corporation' for the sake of convenience of discussion), against whom liability is fastened has preferred MFA 101224 of 2021, the claimant therein has filed MFA 100884 of 2020.

The version of the corporation is that the NC:
2025:KHC-D:15038 HC-KAR compensation granted is high and exorbitant.
On the other hand, the contention of the claimant is that she is entitled to a higher sum.
3. Undisputedly, the claimant sustained bilateral superior and inferior pubic ramus fracture and the said fracture remained mal-united despite the treatment given.
PW2 assessed the disability in respect of whole body as 28%.
But the tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 20%.

While Ms. Vaishali K. Kaladagi submits that the disability taken in respect of whole body is on higher side, Sri Manjunath Jadai, learned counsel for the respondent submits that assessment of the disability by the tribunal is just and proper.

4. Having considered the evidence produced, this Court is of the view that the submission made by learned counsel for the corporation that the disability assessed by the tribunal is on higher side is justifiable.

5. Now coming to the income taken for assessment of compensation, as per the version of the claimant as house NC: 2025:KHC-D:15038 HC-KAR maker she was getting Rs.5,000/- per month and she was contributing the same towards the maintenance of the family.
The tribunal took into consideration the said amount only.
But before this Court learned counsel for the claimant submits that the amount taken as earnings that is Rs.5,000/- per month is on lower side.

When the claimant herself projects that her income is required to be taken as Rs.5,000/- and the tribunal took the same Smt. K. Annapurna vs K. Srinivas on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94666748/
3 into consideration, now the said amount cannot be enhanced.

6. As rightly projected by learned counsel for the claimant, the compensation that was granted by the tribunal towards the expenditure which the claimant would have incurred for food,
nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges, is on lower side.

Admittedly, the claimant must have engaged someone to look after her, while she was at hospital and taking bed rest till the date of recovery and likewise someone would have attended her duties at home during the period of treatment and till the time of recovery.

Thus considering all these aspects this Court is of the view that the NC: 2025:KHC-D:15038 HC-KAR compensation that is granted by the tribunal i.e.
Rs.3,63,000/- can neither be termed to be exorbitant nor on lower side.
The compensation that is granted by the Tribunal is just and reasonable therefore there is no scope either for reduction or for enhancement.
Thus ultimately this Court holds that both the appeals deserve to be dismissed.
7. Resultantly both the appeals stand dismissed.
8. Amount if any in deposit, be transmitted to the concerned tribunal immediately.
